pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.

4. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.

6. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Only carbon dioxide

7. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

8. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

9. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. newton (N)
   D. pascal (Pa)

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.

11. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

12. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Milk souring

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.

2. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.

3. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.

4. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

5. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.

6. A — Glucose and oxygen

7. C — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

8. A — 100 °C

9. C — newton (N)

10. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

11. A — Producers

12. B — Ice melting to water

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Water hardness; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reproduction in plants; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of The Interdependence of Life; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
